newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said that following Thursday's Midday Briefing, exceptionally beginning at 1145/0945 GMT, Commissioners Martin Bangemann and Karel Van Miert would hold a news conference on telecoms liberalisation.

Vale de Almeida said Commission President Jacques Santer and Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok had said during a joint news conference with U.S. President Bill Clinton in The Hague that an agreement on products mutual recognition had not been reached but that there was hope that it would be in the next few days.

Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro would address the European Parliament on the EU position on the Great Lakes and the new Democratic Republic of Congo around 1500/1300 GMT. He said respect of the humanitarian and democratic principles would be at the centre of the Commissioner's intervention.

Asked to react to allegations that the Palestinian government had misused public funds, spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said the Commission would verify the use of European funds. He added that European aid in general was permanently audited and that he was sure the system was solid.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/448: Conference on "Environment and employment", 26/27 May 1997.
- IP/97/449: Promotional and publicity actions for milk and milk products.
- IP/97/452: EU citizenship: Commission report outlines progress and way ahead.
- IP/97/453: Citizens First - Making the Single Market more effective for people.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Regions No 1997-2: Transport infrastructure and road safety: stark contrasts between Member States of the EU.
- Eurostat - Statistic in focus - Energy and industry No 1997-10: Electricity prices for EU households on 1 January 1997: downward trend.
- Partnership - Information bulletin from the Centre for the development of industry.
